summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 92% YoY to INR1,452.8 million and EBITDA margin recovered to 11.9%, but H1 PAT fell 54.8% YoY to INR150 million.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations recovered sharply, up 92% YoY and 42% QoQ to INR1,452.8 million, after a Q1 hit by dispatch and project delays linked to supply chain disruption. EBITDA rose 160.8% YoY to INR172.3 million, with margin at 11.9% versus 5.7% in Q1 FY27. PAT was INR119.7 million, down 33% YoY, and H1 PAT fell 54.8% YoY to INR150 million. Order book stood at INR16,420 million as of October 2026, about 96% defence. Management tied several revenue items to pending government export licences and extensions, which were the main uncertainty in the call.

segments.name: Defence (order book and products)
segments.commentary: About 96% of the INR16,420 million order book. Countermeasures: INR75 crore July 2023 order pending delivery extension, with about INR30 crore LD exposure; INR430 crore October 2025 order with about INR270 crore balance, targeted for completion before FY27 end subject to extension. Chaff and flare revenue of about INR200 crore expected in FY27 from orders in hand.

segments.name: Bulk and industrial explosives
segments.commentary: Management said these are in negative margin. Singareni has extended the existing order and supply continues; about INR80 crore bulk explosives revenue expected this year, with no new major order won yet.

segments.name: Katepally RDX/HMX plant
segments.commentary: Capacity being expanded from 100 tpa to 600 tpa. Water trials have started; commercial production targeted mid-to-end December 2026. Q4 FY27 output around 30 tons, revenue around INR20 crore. About 300 tons targeted for FY28, of which 50-60% expected to be consumed internally.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue target of INR500-600 crore, per CFO, against about INR250 crore in H1.

Gross material margin target of at least 20% for commercial explosives; 20-25% for defence, with defence slightly higher. Management did not reconcile this with the 42% gross margin figure raised by an analyst.
Remaining countermeasures order of about INR270 crore expected to complete before FY27 end, subject to delivery extension.
Capex of about INR32 crore planned for FY27; only about INR11 crore spent in H1 and the balance expected to be completed before FY27 end.
Export ammunition and RDX/HMX licences: 3-4 month approval cycle per order; export price for RDX/HMX cited at $60-70 per kg.
Apollo Micro Systems acquisition of additional 41.33% promoter stake in progress; Board reconstitution expected December 2026.
capex_capacity: Katepally RDX/HMX capacity to rise from 100 tpa to 600 tpa; water trials underway, commercial production targeted mid-to-end December 2026.
H1 FY27 capex about INR11 crore against about INR32 crore planned for FY27, including reconstruction of earlier magazines and logistics.
Nipun mines explosive: production restarted with changes approved by the committee; bulk supplies expected in FY27. Order quantity more than 1 lakh pieces; value not disclosed.
Adrushy and Ulka mine programmes still in qualification; RFQs expected.
No facility for 155 mm artillery shells and no plans to set one up; company does not make TNT.
demand_pricing: Export licence delays are the main constraint: April 2026 export order of INR350 crore still awaiting licence; management said some licences may come next month but would not quantify.
Order-to-order licensing (not product-to-product) confirmed; MOD proposal for product-level licensing not in place.
Supply chain: flare components previously made in-house are now imported after a flare plant accident last year; supply improved over the past two months.
Singareni bulk explosives order extended; no new bulk tenders won, and future volumes depend on new RFPs.
Drone payloads are in trial supply to Air Force and Army; volumes not yet quantified. 40 mm ammunition remains stalled on imported primers and propellants.
Chaff technology transferred by Defence Labs Jodhpur to about 6 companies; management believes Premier is the only supplier so far.

qa_highlights.question: Has the INR75 crore July 2023 countermeasures order received its delivery extension, and when will it complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Extension applied for and expected this quarter; order to be completed this financial year after extension. About INR30 crore LD recovery to be pursued after completion.

qa_highlights.question: How much remains on the INR430 crore October 2025 countermeasures order, and what is H2 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR270 crore balance, expected completed before FY27 end subject to extension. CFO targets INR500-600 crore revenue for H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins declining, and what targets apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Bulk and service contracts are loss-making or squeezed because prices are fixed at tender and cost inflation outpaces escalation; defence margins hit by imported components. Targets: at least 20% gross for commercial, 20-25% for defence. The 42% gross margin figure was disputed by management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RDX/HMX revenue potential for FY28 and the Q4 FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY27 output about 30 tons, revenue about INR20 crore. FY28 target about 300 tons, subject to export licences; 50-60% to be consumed internally. Blended price cited at $60-70 per kg, described as fluid.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company the sole chaff and flare supplier, and what is the FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Five other firms have received the Defence Labs Jodhpur technology; management is not aware of other suppliers. About INR200 crore FY27 revenue expected from chaff and flares on orders in hand.

qa_highlights.question: Will the order book include solid propellants and rocket motors, and what is the Apollo governance outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no breakdown of the order book by product type; said about 60% of the export portion and 40% domestic. Governance expected to stay the same; Board vacancies notified and reconstitution expected in December.

risks_watch: Export licence timing for the INR350 crore April 2026 export order and the 300-ton RDX/HMX FY28 plan; government policy and geopolitics could delay or block them.
Delivery extensions for the countermeasures orders and LD exposure of about INR30 crore on the INR75 crore order.
Gross margin decline and negative-margin bulk and long-term service contracts; reliance on imported flare components.
Bulk explosives: no new orders after Singareni, with visibility beyond FY27 unclear.
Capex execution: only about INR11 crore of about INR32 crore spent in H1.
Apollo acquisition completion and Board reconstitution expected December 2026; governance transition.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q2 recovery and order book, but cautious and sometimes evasive on export licences, pricing, order-book breakdown and product-level margins, deferring to government processes.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin recovered to 11.9% from 5.7% in Q1, but management gave no reconciled margin path and targets a gross material margin of at least 20% for commercial and 20-25% for defence, while bulk contracts are negative-margin and imported flare components squeeze defence margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Katepally RDX/HMX capacity is rising from 100 tpa to 600 tpa (500% increase), water trials have started, and commercial production is targeted mid-to-end December 2026, with about 300 tons targeted for FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets H2 FY27 revenue of INR500-600 crore against about INR250 crore in H1, backed by a INR16,420 million order book (about 96% defence), with about INR200 crore chaff and flare revenue expected in FY27, though export licence timing is the key swing factor.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of about INR32 crore is planned for FY27 with only about INR11 crore spent in H1, and the Katepally expansion is already under way, so management is executing existing programmes rather than signalling a new capex round.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The new H2 FY27 revenue target of INR500-600 crore is conditional on export licences and countermeasures delivery extensions, and management was cautious and evasive on those items, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The INR350 crore April 2026 export order is still awaiting licence with 3-4 month approval cycles, the INR75 crore order needs a delivery extension (about INR30 crore LD exposure), and only INR11 crore of INR32 crore capex is spent in H1.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Drone payloads are in trial supply to Air Force and Army with volumes unquantified, Nipun mines explosive restarted with bulk supplies expected in FY27, and 40 mm ammunition is stalled on imported primers and propellants.

rows.label: Countermeasures order execution (INR430 cr and INR75 cr orders)
rows.why: About INR270 crore balance on the INR430 crore October 2025 order is targeted for completion before FY27 end, and the INR75 crore order is to be completed after an extension applied for this quarter, but both depend on delivery extensions.

rows.label: Export licences for RDX/HMX and ammunition
rows.why: The INR350 crore April 2026 export order still awaits licence, with a 3-4 month approval cycle per order and some licences possibly coming next month, though management would not quantify.

rows.label: Apollo Micro Systems promoter stake acquisition and Board reconstitution
rows.why: Acquisition of an additional 41.33% promoter stake is in progress and Board reconstitution is expected in December 2026, with governance guided to remain the same.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q2 recovery, order book and Katepally ramp, but cautious and evasive on export licences, gross margin (it disputed the 42% figure) and order-book product breakdown; analysts pushed on margins and licence timing.
